'''Felix T. Wieland''' (born 1948) is a German [[biochemist]] and a senior professor at [[Heidelberg University]]. He served as president of the [[German Society for Biochemistry and Molecular Biology]] from 2005 to 2007 and was managing editor of the journal ''[[FEBS Letters]]'' from 2001 to 2021.

Wieland's research concerned the transport of proteins between cell compartments, the analysis of membrane lipids, and the interactions of lipids with proteins. He is an elected member of the [[German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]], the [[European Molecular Biology Organization]] and the [[Academia Europaea]].

== Early life and education ==
Wieland was born in 1948.<ref name="hd2013">{{cite web |title=HMLS Investigator Award for Biochemist Felix Wieland |url=https://www.uni-heidelberg.de/presse/news2013/pm20131206_hmls_award_en.html |publisher=Heidelberg University |date=9 December 2013 |id=Press Release No. 281/2013 |access-date=3 September 2026}}</ref> He is a grandson of [[Heinrich Wieland]] and a nephew of [[Feodor Lynen]] and of [[Theodor Wieland]].<ref name="febs2005">{{cite journal |last=Walma |first=Tine |title=Spotlight on... Felix Wieland |journal=FEBS Letters |volume=579 |issue=9 |year=2005 |page=1898 |doi=10.1016/j.febslet.2005.02.003}}</ref>

He studied chemistry at [[LMU Munich]] from 1969 to 1975. Afterwards, he carried out doctoral research at the [[Max Planck Institute of Biochemistry]] in Martinsried under Lynen between 1975 and 1978.<ref name="leopoldina">{{cite web |title=Prof. Dr. Felix Wieland |url=https://www.leopoldina.org/en/members/member-list/detail/felix-wieland |publisher=German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina |access-date=2 September 2026}}</ref><ref name="febs2005" />

== Career ==
Wieland moved to the [[University of Regensburg]] in 1978. There he held academic posts until 1986 and completed his [[habilitation]] in 1984.<ref name="leopoldina" /> After meeting [[James Rothman]] in 1985, he spent a sabbatical in Rothman's laboratory at [[Stanford University]] from 1986 to 1988, working on the mechanisms of intracellular transport.<ref name="rothman2013">{{cite web |last=Rothman |first=James E. |title=James E. Rothman - Biographical |url=https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2013/rothman/biographical/ |publisher=Nobel Foundation |year=2013 |access-date=9 September 2026}}</ref><ref name="hd2013" />

In 1988, he became a professor at Heidelberg University's Medical Faculty, and held the professorship until 2018, when he was appointed a senior professor of the university.<ref name="leopoldina" /><ref name="hd2021">{{cite web |title=Personalien Oktober 2021 |url=https://www.uni-heidelberg.de/de/newsroom/personalien/archiv-der-personalien/personalien-oktober-2021 |publisher=Heidelberg University |date=1 October 2021 |language=de |access-date=10 September 2026}}</ref><ref name="hd2018">{{cite web |title=Personalien Oktober 2018 |url=https://www.uni-heidelberg.de/de/newsroom/namen-und-nachrichten/archiv/personalien-oktober-2018 |publisher=Heidelberg University |date=24 October 2018 |language=de |access-date=10 September 2026}}</ref>

Wieland joined the editorial board of ''FEBS Letters'' in 1994<ref name="febs2005" /> and was its managing editor from 2001 to 2021.<ref name="febsnet2023">{{cite web |title=Congratulations Felix Wieland, and thank you from FEBS Letters! |url=https://network.febs.org/posts/congratulations-felix-wieland-and-thank-you-from-febs-letters |publisher=FEBS Network |date=3 August 2023 |access-date=2 September 2026}}</ref> He was president of the German Society for Biochemistry and Molecular Biology from 2005 to 2007.<ref name="febsnet2023" />

== Research ==
In his early career, Wieland studied the relative arrangement of the two subunits of yeast [[fatty acid synthase]], which is a large multienzyme complex, by combining antibody crosslinking with negative stain [[electron microscopy]]. Using this approach, he developed a three-dimensional model of the enzyme in 1978.<ref name="maier2010">{{cite journal |last1=Maier |first1=Timm |last2=Leibundgut |first2=Marc |last3=Boehringer |first3=Daniel |last4=Ban |first4=Nenad |title=Structure and function of eukaryotic fatty acid synthases |journal=Quarterly Reviews of Biophysics |volume=43 |issue=3 |year=2010 |pages=373–422 |doi=10.1017/S0033583510000156 |pmid=20731893 |bibcode=2010QRBio..43..373M |hdl=20.500.11850/25501 |hdl-access=free }}</ref>
 
At Regensburg, Wieland worked with Manfred Sumper and Josef Lechner on the cell surface [[glycoprotein]] of the archaeon ''[[Halobacterium salinarum]]''. Through the 1980s he and his colleagues reported the structures of its glycans and aspects of their biosynthesis, sequenced a gene encoding a glycosylated archaeal surface layer protein, and found that glycosylation determines the shape of the cells.<ref name="messner2008">{{cite journal |last1=Messner |first1=Paul |last2=Steiner |first2=Kerstin |last3=Zarschler |first3=Kristof |last4=Schäffer |first4=Christina |title=S-layer nanoglycobiology of bacteria |journal=Carbohydrate Research |volume=343 |issue=12 |year=2008 |pages=1934–1951 |doi=10.1016/j.carres.2007.12.025 |pmid=18336801 |pmc=4381302 }}</ref><ref name="messner1991">{{cite journal |last1=Messner |first1=Paul |last2=Sleytr |first2=Uwe B. |title=Bacterial surface layer glycoproteins |journal=Glycobiology |volume=1 |issue=6 |year=1991 |pages=545–551 |doi=10.1093/glycob/1.6.545 |pmid=1822235 }}</ref> In 1985, with Gerhard Paul and Sumper, he showed that the organism's [[flagellin]]s are glycoproteins.<ref name="jarrell2021">{{cite journal |last1=Jarrell |first1=Ken F. |last2=Albers |first2=Sonja-Verena |last3=Nuno de Sousa Machado |first3=J. |title=A comprehensive history of motility and archaellation in Archaea |journal=FEMS Microbes |volume=2 |year=2021 |article-number=xtab002 |doi=10.1093/femsmc/xtab002 |pmid=37334237 |pmc=10117864 }}</ref>
 
Working with James Rothman, Wieland measured the rate of bulk flow of newly made protein from the [[endoplasmic reticulum]] to the cell surface. Their laboratories developed the budding assay in which purified Golgi membranes and cytosol generate coated vesicles.<ref name="futerman1994">{{cite book |last=Futerman |first=Anthony H. |chapter=Ceramide metabolism compartmentalized in the endoplasmic reticulum and Golgi apparatus |title=Current Topics in Membranes |volume=40 |year=1994 |pages=93–110 |doi=10.1016/S0070-2161(08)60978-8 |pmid=39015509 |pmc=11250679 |isbn=978-0-12-153340-3 }}</ref><ref name="frigerio2007">{{cite journal |last1=Frigerio |first1=Gabriella |last2=Grimsey |first2=Neil |last3=Dale |first3=Martin |last4=Majoul |first4=Irina |last5=Duden |first5=Rainer |title=Two human ARFGAPs associated with COP-I-coated vesicles |journal=Traffic |volume=8 |issue=11 |year=2007 |pages=1644–1655 |doi=10.1111/j.1600-0854.2007.00631.x |pmid=17760859 |pmc=2171037 }}</ref> Afterwards, his work focused on the [[COPI]] coat, which packages proteins into vesicles for transport between the [[Golgi apparatus]] and the endoplasmic reticulum.<ref name="arakel2018">{{cite journal |last1=Arakel |first1=Eric C. |last2=Schwappach |first2=Blanche |title=Formation of COPI-coated vesicles at a glance |journal=Journal of Cell Science |volume=131 |issue=5 |year=2018 |page=jcs209890 |doi=10.1242/jcs.209890 |pmid=29535154 |hdl=21.11116/0000-0000-F94F-0 |hdl-access=free }}</ref> In 1999 he reported the reconstitution of COPI vesicle budding from a minimal set of purified components.<ref name="febs2005" /> Later with John Briggs, he produced a molecular model of the coat by using reconstituted vesicles.<ref name="arakel2017">{{cite journal |last1=Arakel |first1=Eric C. |last2=Schwappach |first2=Blanche |title=Vesicles: Looking inside the cell |journal=eLife |volume=6 |year=2017 |article-number=e33650 |doi=10.7554/eLife.33650 |doi-access=free |pmid=29202927 |pmc=5716659 }}</ref>
 
Wieland, Britta Brügger, and Wolf-Dieter Lehmann developed a nano-electrospray mass spectrometric method for quantifying membrane lipids at low picomole amounts.<ref name="han2005">{{cite journal |last1=Han |first1=Xianlin |last2=Gross |first2=Richard W. |title=Shotgun lipidomics: electrospray ionization mass spectrometric analysis and quantitation of cellular lipidomes directly from crude extracts of biological samples |journal=Mass Spectrometry Reviews |volume=24 |issue=3 |year=2005 |pages=367–412 |doi=10.1002/mas.20023 |pmid=15389848 |bibcode=2005MSRv...24..367H }}</ref> Wieland and Brügger also examined how proteins and lipids interact in membranes,<ref name="leopoldina" /> and, in 2012, reported that a single molecule of one specific species of [[sphingomyelin]] binds the transmembrane domain of the p24 coat subunit and regulates formation of the COPI coat.<ref name="bankaitis2012">{{cite journal |last1=Bankaitis |first1=Vytas A. |last2=Garcia-Mata |first2=Rafael |last3=Mousley |first3=Carl J. |title=Golgi membrane dynamics and lipid metabolism |journal=Current Biology |volume=22 |issue=10 |year=2012 |pages=R414–R424 |doi=10.1016/j.cub.2012.03.004 |pmid=22625862 |pmc=4059015 |bibcode=2012CBio...22.R414B }}</ref>

* 2001 - Heinrich Wieland Prize, Boehringer Ingelheim Stiftung<ref>{{cite web|title=List of Heinrich Wieland Prize Laureates since 1964|url=https://boehringer-ingelheim-stiftung.de/fileadmin/content/bistiftung/downloads/pdf/HWP/HWP_List_of_Laureates_2025_quick_search.pdf|website=Boehringer Ingelheim Stiftung|access-date=15 September 2026}}</ref>
* 2003 - Elected member, [[German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina|Leopoldina]]<ref name="leopoldina" />
* 2006 - Feldberg Foundation Prize<ref>{{cite web|url=https://feldbergfoundation.org/prizewinners/|title=Feldberg Foundation - Prize Winners|access-date=15 September 2026}}</ref>
* 2011 - Elected member, Academia Europaea<ref name="ae">{{cite web |title=Felix Wieland |url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Wieland_Felix |publisher=Academia Europaea |access-date=2 September 2026}}</ref>
